title: DGIP - Passport application process
section: Step 1 – Arrival of Applicant at Customer Service Counter
text: Step 1 – Arrival of Applicant at Customer Service Counter. The applicant will approach the customer service counter at Regional Passport Office. The applicant will be guided about the process flow of the System for applying for the passport. After having the requisite documents, the applicant will be guided to the Token Counter.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
section: Step 2 – Capturing of Photograph + Token Issuance with QR Code
text: Step 2 – Capturing of Photograph + Token Issuance with QR Code. The applicant will produce the original CNIC/Smart-Card/NICOP or Children Registration Certificate (CRC)/B-Form, in case of below 18 years of age, along with its copies . The Official will proceed with capturing of applicant’s data i.e. photograph, CNIC Number, application type etc. QR Code based token will be issued to the applicant. The applicant should check his details on token i.e. Application type, Priority type, CNIC/CRC number . In case of any discrepancy, he should immediately report to an official at the token counter, otherwise, the applicant has to go through twice to all the subsequent stages.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
text: Step 3 – Biometric Data Capture (Finger Prints). The applicant after obtaining token will approach the Biometric Counter as soon as his token number appears at Biometric Capturing Counter. The official at the Counter will capture his right thumb, right index finger, Left Thumb and Left index finger impressions.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
text: Step 4 – Data Entry. The applicant will move to the Data Entry Counters as soon as his token number appears on the Counter. The official will enter all the required data of the applicant while the data entry screen will also be visible to the Applicant. In case of any modification in data, the Applicant should guide the official accordingly. After the data entry is completed Data Entry Form will be printed by the operator and will be presented to the Applicant for rechecking/verification. The applicant will verify all its contents by signing the form. The form will be delivered to the applicant for further processing.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
section: Step 5 – Verification as per Office Record (ECL/BL)
text: Step 5 – Verification as per Office Record (ECL/BL). The applicant will approach the ECL/BL Desk having Form. The verification against Exit Control List (ECL) and Black List (BL) will be carried out and official on the desk will affix clearance stamp on the data form after checking the record. The persons borne on ECL or BL, their passport process would be stopped here until its removal from such lists, as per rules/SOP.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
section: Step 6 – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director
text: Step 6 – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director. Finally, the applicant will appear before Assistant Director / Officer In-charge when his token number appears on the decision counter, along with all the relevant documents and Data Form. The Assistant Director/ Officer In-charge will interview the applicant and satisfy himself with respect to the National Status/credibility of the applicant. Upon his satisfaction, he will allow, “Go ahead” the case, otherwise he can ask for additional documents. If required he will refer the case to Security Agency for determination of National Status of the applicant as citizen of Pakistan.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
section: Step 6 – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director
text: Step 6 – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director. The Assistant Director will defer the case of Applicant below 18 years of age and will hand over the printed form to the applicant for attestation of his data form, from a Government Gazetted officer. The attester will have to write his/her CNIC No./ Contact No. besides affixing by-name official stamp on the form. On production of data form (duly attested) the deferred token of minor will be allowed go-ahead. After allowing go-ahead by Assistant Director, the applicant may leave the Passport Office, as the process is complete, by taking token generated at Step 2.

title: DGIP - Passport application process
section: Step 6 – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director
text: Step 6 – Interview & Decision by Assistant Director. In case the matter is deferred due to some additional documents or case referred to the Security Agency for determination of National Status by the Assistant Director/ Officer In-charge, the applicant may also leave the office, as the remaining process will be completed upon receipt of documents/clearance report from Security Agency. The applicant would be informed upon receipt of clearance report telephonically.

text: Q-15- What is the difference between Machine Readable Passport (MRP) and e-Passport?. Answer: Both are issued by the Government of Pakistan, but they offer different features and benefits. This comparison highlights the distinctions and advantages of each type. Machine-Readable Passport (MRP): Introduced in 2004 | e-Passport: Launched in March 2021.

title: DGIP - Frequently asked questions
section: Q-15- What is the difference between Machine Readable Passport (MRP) and e-Passport?
text: Q-15- What is the difference between Machine Readable Passport (MRP) and e-Passport?. Machine-Readable Passport (MRP): Machine-Readable Zone (MRZ): MRPs include an MRZ that can be read by optical scanners at passport control. This zone contains the passport holder’s personal information in a standardized format. Data Page: The data page includes the holder's photo, name, nationality, date of birth, and other relevant information. Security Features: MRPs have various security features, such as watermarks, holograms, and UV-visible elements to prevent counterfeiting. Paper-Based: Primarily a physical document without embedded electronic components. | e-Passport: Embedded Microchip: This contains a microchip embedded in the passport cover, which stores the holder's personal data, including biometric information such as fingerprints and a digital photograph. Enhanced Security: Offers advanced security features including digital signatures, encryption, and public key infrastructure (PKI) to prevent unauthorized access and tampering. Contactless Communication: The microchip can be read by RFID readers at passport control, facilitating quicker and more secure verification. Comprehensive Biometric Data: Stores more detailed biometric data than MRPs, enhancing identity verification processes..

title: DGIP - Frequently asked questions
section: Q-15- What is the difference between Machine Readable Passport (MRP) and e-Passport?
text: Q-15- What is the difference between Machine Readable Passport (MRP) and e-Passport?. Machine-Readable Passport (MRP): Benefits of MRP | e-Passport: Benefits of e-Passport. Machine-Readable Passport (MRP): Global Acceptance: Recognized and accepted globally, facilitating international travel. Cost-Effective: Generally, less expensive to produce and renew compared to e-passports. Basic Security: Adequate security features that meet international standards, ensuring the document's authenticity and integrity. | e-Passport: Enhanced Security: The embedded microchip and encryption make e-passports significantly more secure against forgery and identity theft. Faster Processing: The contactless chip allows for quicker processing at automated border control gates, reducing waiting times. Improved Verification: The inclusion of biometric data provides a more reliable method of verifying the passport holder’s identity, improving border security..

Summary : While both MRPs and e-Passports serve the primary function of facilitating international travel and verifying identity, e-Passports offer enhanced security, faster processing times, and more reliable identity verification through biometric data. MRPs, on the other hand, are more cost-effective and widely recognized, making them a suitable option for travelers seeking a basic yet secure travel document. As technology and security needs evolve, e-passports represent a forward-looking solution that aligns with global trends in digital security and border management.

title: DGIP - e-Passport
text: What is e-Passport?. The e-Passport is a highly secure travel document. It has an electronic chip embedded in one of the passport pages, which will be used to store biometric information about the holder. The chip contains data that will verify the passport holder’s identity and will include the biometrics of the passport holder, the personal data found on the data page of the passport, a unique identification number and a digital signature. An e-passport has a contactless (NFC) chip on it which means that those passports can be read electronically. The newly launched e-Passports in Pakistan are in compliance with the United Nations’ ICAO standards.

It will also help eliminate all the hurdles in the ongoing manual system and will aid Pakistani applicants to process online applications conveniently. Since the e-Passport carries out various forms of security checks, extending benefits to overseas Pakistanis will ultimately benefit the country.

title: Passport Rules 2021
text: Page 25. Provided that diplomatic passports shall be held by the above categories of persons so long as they hold the prescribed offices. If they cease to hold such offices they may be required to surrender the diplomatic passports within 30-days of ceasing to hold their offices except items at serial numbers (a) to (d) of the item (1) of this schedule. (2) Spouses of diplomatic passport holders .—Spouses of diplomatic passport holders shall be entitled for diplomatic passport. He or she will hold diplomatic passport as long as his or her spouse retains the prescribed office. ———— SCHEDULE – V [See Rule 7 (d)] Ordinary gratis passport .—Such passports shal l be issued to the following categories of persons;
